payload.name: Preserve all explicit feelings in extraction
payload.description: When a message explicitly states multiple feelings or attributes about the same activity or subject, include all of them in the extracted memory candidate instead of selecting only one.
content: During candidate extraction, if the source text explicitly lists multiple distinct feelings, preferences, or attributes about the same subject or activity (e.g., 'exciting and free-feeling'), capture every listed element in the memory content. Do not drop any explicit descriptor even if one seems more salient; paraphrase only to combine them concisely.

solves: Extraction candidates often drop one of multiple explicitly stated feelings about the same activity, losing a claim. The rule: when a message lists multiple distinct feelings or attributes, retain all explicit descriptors. This applies to any future extraction where a single subject has several explicit evaluative terms.
